reports.title: Eversource Energy Reports Third Quarter 2026 Results

lines: The Company is updating its 2026 non-GAAP recurring earnings guidance to be in the range of $4.62 per share1 and $4.70 per share1 reflecting an increased midpoint of $4.66 per share1.

It also reaffirms its cumulative long-term earnings per share growth rate within the range of 5 to 7 percent through 2030, using the aforementioned revised 2026 non-GAAP earnings guidance midpoint of $4.66 per share1 as the base year.

Q3 2026 EARNINGS REPORT November 5, 2026 Recent Highlights Recurring EPS of $0.92; in line with guidance Revolution Wind Update FERC ROE & Refund; line of sight into timing CL&P Rate Case progress continues Massachusetts AMI > 500K meters installed Transmission project TIDE selected for ISO - NE LTTP Eversource wins DREAM grid modernization DOE grant Named one of America’s Best Companies by TIME 5
Approved incremental investments during and beyond this forecast period: $700 Million TIDE (~$400m 2027 - 30)

desk.headline: Revenue down 7.5% to $2.98bn; EPS $0.92 missed $0.97 estimate; 2026 range narrowed to $4.62-4.70
results: Recurring EPS fell to $0.92 from $1.19 a year ago and missed the $0.97 estimate; there were no one-off items this quarter, so GAAP EPS was also $0.92 (vs $0.99).
Operating revenue fell 7.5% to $2.98bn, partly because the Aquarion water business was sold on 30 June 2026 and no longer contributes.

Transmission earnings slipped to $182m after regulator FERC cut the allowed return on equity to 9.57% from 10.57%; distribution earnings fell 9% as Connecticut's regulator disallowed some storm costs.
The gas business lost $43m in the quarter, mainly because a new Massachusetts rate design shifts revenue between quarters, plus higher depreciation.
Over nine months, GAAP EPS was $2.67 after charges for the Aquarion sale ($0.30), offshore wind ($0.43) and FERC refunds ($0.12).

guidance.summary: Eversource narrowed its 2026 recurring EPS range to $4.62-4.70 (was $4.52-4.72), lifting the midpoint to $4.66, and kept its 5-7% yearly EPS growth target through 2030, now aiming for the upper half by 2028.

points: Management blamed the weaker quarter on the FERC return cut, a roughly $40m Connecticut storm-cost disallowance, the Aquarion sale and a higher tax rate.
It is appealing the FERC refund order in court and warned accounting rules may force it to book the full refund before a ruling; meeting the May 2027 refund deadline will be hard.
Credit metrics improved (S&P FFO/debt 15.4%, Moody's 16.1%) and no new shares are needed near term thanks to $1.7bn of Aquarion proceeds.
Revolution Wind is complete, which management said sharply cuts the risk of further offshore wind costs.
About $1.1bn of storm costs should be securitised, with Connecticut cash expected around mid-2027; the Connecticut rate case decision is expected around mid-2027.
call.source: Earnings presentation (Exhibit 99.3); call transcript (The Motley Fool via Webull, 5 Nov 2026); Earnings Whispers call summary (5 Nov 2026)

watch: FERC's decision on the new transmission return (effective 30 Nov) and the court appeal of the refund order
Whether a large FERC refund charge has to be booked before the appeal is decided
Connecticut storm-cost securitisation ruling (expected late January) and progress on the CL&P rate case
